transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Well, what brings me in is... I just keep forgetting things I really shouldn't. It's becoming a bit of a problem. Like, I'll completely miss my heart follow-up appointments, or I'll forget to call the clinic back when I'm supposed to. Even just doing stuff around the house, I'll go to start a repair job and realize I showed up without the right tools. I just can't seem to keep things straight lately.
Have you had this kind of forgetfulness since you were a child?

Well, yeah, it goes way back. I mean, even as a boy in grade school, I was always the kid who just couldn't stay in his seat. I'd, uh, I'd blurt out answers all the time, and I got plenty of notes sent home to my parents for talking too much. So I've always been a bit all over the place, I guess.
Were you having these attention and distractibility problems as a child, before age 12?

To be honest, I'm not really sure about the attention part. That was a long time ago. I mainly just remember the, uh, getting in trouble for not sitting still and the talking, like I said. But as far as being distracted or not paying attention... I really couldn't tell you if I had problems with that back then.
When did these memory and organization problems first start to become a real problem for you?

It's really been a problem for about a year and two months now. That's when I had a bit of a cardiac scare, and I had to cut way back on all the walking and the different projects I used to do. Those things used to burn off my energy and keep me settled, I think. Since I had to stop doing them as much, keeping things straight has been a lot harder.
Have you been feeling depressed or down most days for the past couple of weeks?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, sure, it gets a little frustrating dealing with all this restless energy and not being able to do my projects like I used to... but I don't feel depressed or down. My mood has been fine, really.
Did you have these kinds of restlessness or fidgeting problems before age 12?

Yeah, I definitely did. Even back as a boy in grade school, I was always the kid who just couldn't stay in his seat. I'd blurt out answers in class, and, well, I got a lot of notes sent home to my parents for talking too much. So the restlessness has really been there a long time.

latest_inference.note: Childhood-onset hyperactivity/restlessness is confirmed and current symptoms are longstanding; this makes ADHD/hyperkinetic disorder most likely and rules out primary depression, generalized anxiety, and mild cognitive disorder as the main explanation.
